None of this was inevitable.
It only looks inevitable now because it worked.

Every time we organised, something permanent was locked in.
And every time we stopped, it was slowly wound back.

What you are looking at is not a timeline. It is a warning and a reminder.
Rights do not age out. They get defended or they get diluted.

History is not nostalgia.
It is proof of what happens when professionals act together.

If you want the next chapter to exist,
it requires the same thing the last ones did.

Join PA today.

Professionals Australia's Workplace Advice and Support Team has won back $3 million in unpaid entitlements for members this year… and $900K in the last fortnight alone.

That’s real money back in members’ pockets.

Where it always should have been.

PA member Victoria Wansink says it best: 

ACT Government Scientists would rather be in the lab protecting the community but until the ACT Government comes back with a fair offer, Professionals Australia members will keep fighting for safe workplaces.

ACT Government Scientists are taking action and making news.

These are the experts entering drug labs, handling toxic chemicals, and facing serious risk every day, without fair pay or proper recognition.

They don’t want to be protesting. They want to be in the lab, protecting the community.

But until the ACT Government listens, the action will continue.

ACT Government Scientists just made history, walking off the job in their first ever strike and marching on the ACT Legislative Assembly for fair hazard pay. 

After a decade of real wage cuts and months of government silence, they’re done being told there’s money for everything except their safety. They enter meth labs, handle fentanyl and other toxic chemicals, and keep the community safe.

All without the allowance already paid to comparable frontline roles. 

The turnout was huge and the message  @was clear: recognise the risks, put a fair offer on the table, or expect more action from united workers who won’t back down.

Michele O'Neil and Sally McManus are leaving the ACTU this year after 8 years running Australia's union movement together, the first women to hold both top jobs at the same time in its 99 year history.
 
A lot changed under their leadership.
Wages moved in sectors that had been stuck for years, the gender pay gap fell to its lowest point on record, and membership, which had been going backwards for decades, started climbing again.
 
They've said the next generation of leaders needs to be ready for what's coming, including AI's impact on jobs. That's already a live issue for our members, and one we'll keep fighting on long after this handover.
 
Professionals Australia is an ACTU affiliate. We admire the 8 years Michele and Sally spent standing up for working people, and we want to thank them for it.

"I thought it was just me."

It almost never is. Ashley found that out when she stopped carrying it alone and realised her whole team was dealing with the same thing, and that together, with their union, it could change.

Join Professionals Australia.

Your employer can thank you all they like. Gratitude is free.

What actually protects your pay, your hours and your conditions isn't appreciation. It's what's written into your agreement, in black and white, and enforceable. Claps fade. Clauses hold.

Professionals Australia is how STEM professionals get those clauses written and defended.
PA Tech member Millie from Atlassian says union membership means workers can bargain to lock in the rights they rely on, rather than hoping companies keep offering them.

We want you for an HSR at Snowy Hydro 2.0!

To nominate, email new lead organiser Jonathan Farry at jfarry@pa.org.au

A Health and Safety Representative is elected by their workmates to speak for them on safety. HSRs get trained. They must be consulted before changes that affect health and safety. They can inspect the site, investigate hazards, issue provisional improvement notices and direct unsafe work to stop.

Strong HSRs can turn a site around. That is exactly why Webuild fought so hard to keep white collar workers out of the process, refusing to negotiate work groups for engineers, supervisors, surveyors and technical staff. We took it to SafeWork NSW. The regulator determined separate work groups across Polo Flat, Tantangara, Lobs Hole and Marica.

We won the right. Now let’s use it! #snowyhydro #safetyfirst #HSR #nsw #ausunions

The Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) runs the systems that keep electricity and gas flowing to millions of homes and businesses. The engineers, analysts and specialists who do that work have just sent their employer a clear message.

For the second time, AEMO employees have voted down the proposed enterprise agreement.

Two offers. Two rejections. One message management can't miss: this workforce is live, and it will not be pressured into accepting less than it's worth.

When professionals stand together, they control the switch. Workers held the line, staying united, to reject management's offer.

This is what collective power looks like!

Progress has been made in the workplace presence dispute at Sydney Trains, with proposed improvements to hybrid working arrangements now on the table.

The proposed changes include expanded access to standard hybrid working arrangements for more employees, increased opportunities for individual hybrid working arrangements, and other improvements to the current framework.

Professionals Australia members at Sydney Trains are encourage to attend the members meeting this Thursday for an important update and provide feedback before negotiations progress further.
